title: Cotangent bundles of smooth homogeneous quotients as associated bundles
statement: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], $G$ a smooth connected affine $F$-group scheme of finite type [def-sc-group-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], and $H\subseteq G$ a smooth closed subgroup [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]. Suppose the fppf quotient is represented by a separated finite-type $F$-scheme $Q$, and $q:G\to Q$ is a right $H$-torsor: it is faithfully flat and finitely presented and $(g,h)\mapsto(g,gh)$ identifies $G\times_FH$ with $G\times_QG$. Write $o=q(e)$, $\mathfrak g=T_eG$, $\mathfrak h=T_eH$ for tangent spaces (vectors are lifts of the indicated point to $F[\varepsilon]/(\varepsilon^2)$), and $V=(\mathfrak g/\mathfrak h)^\vee=\operatorname{Hom}_F(\mathfrak g/\mathfrak h,F)$. Give $\mathfrak g/\mathfrak h$ the $H$-action induced by conjugation and $V$ its contragredient action: $(h\lambda)(v)=\lambda(\operatorname{Ad}(h^{-1})v)$. All actions are group-scheme actions, hence identities after every commutative $F$-algebra extension. For a finite-dimensional rational $H$-module $W$, let $G\times^H W$ denote the vector bundle obtained by faithfully flat descent of $G\times W$ with $(g,w)\cdot h=(gh,h^{-1}w)$; its sheaf is the descent of $\mathcal O_G\otimes_FW$. Then $Q$ is smooth, $q$ is smooth, and the differential of $q$ induces an $H$-equivariant exact sequence $0\to\mathfrak h\to\mathfrak g\to T_oQ\to0$. There is a $G$-equivariant isomorphism of vector bundles $$\Omega^1_{Q/F}\simeq G\times^H V,$$ where the left side denotes the bundle whose sheaf of sections is the relative differential sheaf [def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf]. If $d=\dim_F V$, the sheaf of sections of $G\times^H\bigwedge^d V$ is canonically isomorphic to $\bigwedge^d\Omega^1_{Q/F}$ [def-sc-sheaf-exterior-power]. In particular $\Omega^1_{Q/F}$ is locally free of constant rank $d$ and $Q$ is of pure dimension $d$. These assertions include $d=0$ and hold in every characteristic.

source.place: Proposition 7.15, printed pp.142--143, for smooth quotient maps; Section 18c, printed pp.389--390, especially 18.11 and the proof of 18.14, for reconstruction from the stabilizer fibre. Vector-bundle and exterior-power extension written by Q79. Brion--Kumar Section 2.1, printed pp.63--64, associated rational B-modules, is supporting reference (WANTED locally; author PDF read online).

proof.text: The quotient sheaf has the left $G$-action induced by multiplication on $G$; multiplication commutes with the right $H$-action, so it acts on right cosets, and representability makes this a scheme action. The map $q$ is equivariant. The torsor isomorphism identifies the base change of $q$ along itself with $G\times_F H\to G$. This projection is smooth by smooth base change, since $H/F$ is smooth. Smoothness descends along the faithfully flat, quasi-compact surjection $q$, so $q$ is smooth. (A finitely presented map is quasi-compact.) Applying smooth source descent to $G\xrightarrow{q}Q\to\operatorname{Spec}F$ now shows that $Q/F$ is smooth: the composite is the given smooth structure morphism of $G$, and $q$ is flat, surjective and locally finitely presented.

source.place: Proposition 7.15, printed pp.142--143, torsor cartesian square; Stacks descent.tex Tags 02VL and 05B5

proof.text: The fibre of $q$ over $o$ is $H$: pull back the torsor isomorphism along the identity in its first coordinate. Thus a dual-number tangent vector at $e$ maps to zero at $o$ exactly when it factors uniquely through $H$. This proves injectivity of $\mathfrak h\to\mathfrak g$ and identifies its image with the kernel. Given a dual-number vector at $o$, formal smoothness of $q$ lifts the diagram with closed subscheme $\operatorname{Spec}F$ mapping to $e$ across $\operatorname{Spec}F\subset\operatorname{Spec}F[\varepsilon]/(\varepsilon^2)$. Therefore $dq_e$ is surjective. Tangent maps are linear by the tangent-space definition. Consequently $\mathfrak g/\mathfrak h\simeq T_oQ$. The smooth differential sheaves are finite locally free; tangent--differential-fibre duality makes all three tangent spaces finite-dimensional and identifies $E_o:=o^*\Omega^1_{Q/F}$ canonically with $(T_oQ)^\vee$, hence with $V$, by the finite-dimensional double-dual evaluation map.

source.place: Tags 0B2C, 0B2D, 0B2F; morphisms.tex Tag 02G1; more-morphisms.tex Tag 02H0 (lifting definition)

proof.text: The stabilizer of $o$ is $H$ as a group scheme, by the same fibre identification. For every $F$-algebra $A$, $h\in H(A)$ and infinitesimal $x\in G(A[\varepsilon])$ at $e$, the equality of cosets gives $q(hxh^{-1})=h\,q(x)$. Differentiation gives $dq_e\operatorname{Ad}(h)=d(L_h)_o dq_e$. Conjugation preserves $H$, so it preserves $\mathfrak h$. This proves the equivariance of the exact sequence for conjugation on its first two terms and the stabilizer differential on its last term. Under the duality of step 2, the forward cotangent action of $h$ on $E_o$ is the dual of $d(L_{h^{-1}})_o$, so $(h\lambda)(v)=\lambda(\operatorname{Ad}(h^{-1})v)$. The calculations are valid over $A$: differential base change identifies the fibres there with scalar extensions of the fibres over $F$, and finite-dimensional duals commute with scalar extension, as is checked on a basis. Thus these are identities of representations, including nonreduced test algebras.

source.place: Tags 01UV and 01V0; varieties.tex Tag 0B2D; explicit conjugation identity written here

proof.text: Put $E=\Omega^1_{Q/F}$. The automorphism $b:G\times Q\to G\times Q$, $(g,z)\mapsto(g,gz)$, over $G$ has inverse $(g,z)\mapsto(g,g^{-1}z)$. Differential base change identifies $\Omega^1_{(G\times Q)/G}$ with $\operatorname{pr}_Q^*E$. The differential map for $b$ and its inverse therefore give an isomorphism $a^*E\simeq\operatorname{pr}_Q^*E$, where $a(g,z)=gz$; on a fibre its inverse is the forward action $g\cdot\alpha=(dL_{g^{-1}})^*\alpha$. Composition holds because on each generator $du$ both composite differential maps send $du$ to the differential of the composite pullback of $u$. Restrict the forward isomorphism along $g\mapsto(g,o)$. It gives an isomorphism $\theta:\mathcal O_G\otimes_F E_o\xrightarrow{\sim}q^*E$, $\theta_g(v)=g\cdot v$. This constructs the map as an algebraic bundle isomorphism over $G$, not just at field-valued points.

source.place: Tags 01UV (unique map on differentials) and 01V0 (relative differential base change); explicit action automorphism argument

proof.text: For the $H$-representation $E_o=V$ of step 3, $\theta_{gh}(h^{-1}v)=(gh)\cdot(h^{-1}\cdot v)=g\cdot v=\theta_g(v)$. This is an equality of maps over $G\times H$, by the composition identity in step 4. On $G\times_QG\simeq G\times H$ it says exactly that $\theta$ respects the descent datum $(g,v)\cdot h=(gh,h^{-1}v)$ and the canonical descent datum of $q^*E$. FPQC descent for quasi-coherent modules is fully faithful and effective, and reflects finite local freeness of a specified rank. Hence $\theta$ and its inverse descend to the asserted isomorphism $G\times^H V\simeq E$. For $k\in G(A)$ one has $\theta_{kg}(v)=(kg)\cdot v=k\cdot\theta_g(v)$; full faithfulness, applied after the base change $G\times G\to G\times Q$ as well, descends this equality and proves $G$-equivariance. The same descent statement shows $E$ is locally free of constant rank $d=\dim_FV$, since its pullback is $\mathcal O_G\otimes_F V$.

source.place: Tag 023T, proposition-fpqc-descent-quasi-coherent; Tag 05B2, lemma-finite-locally-free-descends; Milne 18.11 and proof of 18.14, printed pp.389--390 (line-bundle model)

proof.text: For a finite locally free sheaf, exterior powers commute with module pullback: on an open where a basis $e_1,\ldots,e_d$ is chosen, send $1\otimes(e_{i_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge e_{i_r})$ to $(1\otimes e_{i_1})\wedge\cdots\wedge(1\otimes e_{i_r})$. Increasing-index wedges form bases on both sides; the inverse sends those basis wedges back. The maps agree under a change of basis by multilinearity and the alternating relations, so glue canonically. Apply this to $E$ and the isomorphism $\theta$. The resulting isomorphism $\mathcal O_G\otimes_F\bigwedge^d V\simeq q^*\bigwedge^d E$ intertwines descent: the identity in step 5, on a pure wedge, is the wedge of that identity on its $d$ entries. FPQC full faithfulness descends it and its inverse, proving the claimed canonical top-wedge isomorphism. For $d=0$ both constructions give $\mathcal O_Q$ and the map sends $1$ to $1$.

source.place: Tag 023T; explicit finite-basis exterior-power computation from def-sc-sheaf-exterior-power

proof.text: At every point $x$ of the smooth $F$-scheme $Q$, the differential-rank/fibre-dimension theorem gives an affine neighbourhood on which the differential module is free of rank $\dim_xQ$. Its rank is also $d$ by step 5; taking its fibre at $x$ shows $\dim_xQ=d$. Thus $Q/F$ is smooth of relative dimension $d$, which by the smooth-relative-dimension convention means its nonempty fibre $Q$ is equidimensional of dimension $d$. This is the asserted pure dimension. The point $o$ ensures $Q$ is nonempty. No step divides by the characteristic or uses connectedness of $H$. In particular a finite smooth $H$, $H=1$, $H=G$, and $d=0$ are all included.

Step 1 follows Milne 7.15 (printed pp.142-143): the torsor square makes the base change of q along q equal to G×H→G, which is smooth by lem-pc-proper-base-change(2). lem-trf-smooth-fpqc-base-descent then applies to q, since q is flat, surjective and quasi-compact (finite presentation gives quasi-compact). lem-sbc source descent applies to Q/F. Step 2: the fibre of q over o is H, which gives the kernel and injectivity; formal smoothness lifts e and gives surjectivity; finite dimension comes from lem-ag finite local freeness plus rational tangent-differential duality. Step 3: q(hxh^{-1})=hq(x), so the cotangent action is contragredient to Ad. It is checked over every F-algebra by differential base change. Step 4: the automorphism b over G, def-a1 and base change give θ: O_G⊗E_o≅q^*E. Step 5: θ_{gh}(h^{-1}v)=θ_g(v) is the descent datum, matching Milne's 18.13 convention (gb,χ(b^{-1})x); lem-pc-fpqc-descent (1) and (2) give descent of θ, G-equivariance and rank d.
